headline: BRICS delegate admits 5-point action plan is actually just his list of grievances against his landlord
body:
Q: Reports suggest the new five-point action plan presented at the BRICS summit has caused significant confusion among international observers. Can you explain the genesis of these points?

A: Look, I was under a lot of pressure to finalize the agenda before the morning plenary, and my laptop charger had died. I opened my Notes app, and the only thing I had written down was a draft email to my landlord about the leaky tap, the faulty geyser, the missing floor tiles, the unreasonable hike in security deposit, and the persistent noise from the apartment above.

Q: Are you saying the official five-point roadmap for economic cooperation is identical to a dispute over a rental agreement in a South Delhi apartment complex?

A: Exactly. Point one, 'Immediate restoration of structural integrity,' is obviously about the balcony railings, but the delegates seemed to interpret it as a profound commitment to geopolitical stability. When I proposed 'Aggressive escalation in case of non-compliance,' they all stood up and applauded for ten minutes. It was very awkward.

Q: Does it concern you that major powers are now drafting national policies based on your grievances regarding a malfunctioning kitchen faucet?

A: Frankly, it’s a relief. For the first time in years, the local housing society isn't replying to my emails, but suddenly the entire global bloc is forming a committee to address my 'infrastructure concerns.' Honestly, I'm just hoping they can get someone to fix the geyser by Friday.
caption: When the diplomatic deadline hits and your landlord is still ignoring your messages, you improvise. A true lesson in professional multitasking. #BRICS #Diplomacy #RealEstate #InternationalRelations (satire)
igHook: Have you ever accidentally used your personal to-do list for a professional presentation?
